decisions_recap: Rungs 1 and 2 never import the OCR seam, so 'exact text and zero OCR calls' is structural, not tested-in only.
A multi-quad annotation is ONE region with several rects; a malformed/no-QuadPoints annotation falls back to its rect rather than being dropped.
Exact text is intersected in page-normalized space (normalizeTextBoxes first).
The colour mask is a pure module (Worker is a perf follow-up); its thresholds, minimums and line merge are the spec's.
group highlights via an optional layer on NewHighlight (default individual); the import passes group and RLS enforces leader-only (RULE-04).
The review derives its rows from candidates with overrides in state (no seed effect); nothing commits unaccepted.
F5 client half is one writeRows transaction; the server fan-out is 001/007, untouched.
follow_up_tasks: Run the plan's Gate with a real Acrobat-annotated PDF fixture against the parser and the review (a human/fixture task; the zero-OCR property is already structural).
Wire an import entry point into the document-view route: rasterize the page, choose the rung, run the mask (ideally in a Worker), and render ImportReview — the route that 009-016 all left unmounted.
Move the colour mask into a Worker once a page raster exists (spec §5.4's suggestion; pure today).
021's server side: the leader import fans out as ONE broadcast (F5); 001's trigger and 007's channel already batch, so confirm it under a 40-highlight import when the live stack is in the loop.
Reuse the same review model for 013's promotion flow if the UX overlaps.

postscript.note: The first follow-up is partly done. src/features/highlight/utils/annotation-quads.real.test.ts builds a real PDF with pdf-lib (text + a two-quad /Highlight + a Square) and reads it back through the real pdfjs annotation and text layers: rung 1 yields two normalized rects and the exact text-layer text with confidence 1 and no OCR. This also confirmed the parser's assumption that pdfjs v6 reports `quadPoints` as a flat number array (a real multi-quad highlight does not collapse to its rect). viewportLike() was extracted from use-import-source so the real pdfjs viewport seam is covered. A genuine Acrobat-exported fixture remains the manual check.
